builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Low-Bit GDN Recurrent-State Quantization: Global Gradient-aware Allocation and Pure-Write Sliding Windows
summary: The method replaces uniform low-bit quantization of the linear-attention (GDN) recurrent state with a model-wide mixed-precision allocation driven by quantization residuals and gradient sensitivity to future loss, plus an FP8 sliding window that keeps recent writes unquantized until they age out. Its cost is implementation complexity: per-head bit-width allocation, a separate FP8 write path that must be propagated through the full state transition, and merged on window exit, all of which require custom inference code for a specific architecture. It can fail when the deployed model is not a GDN-style linear-attention model, when gradient-sensitivity estimates do not transfer across tasks, or when the window merge introduces transition artifacts not covered by the seven evaluated tasks.
rationale: The technique targets only GDN linear-attention models and demands custom state-management inference code, so it is relevant to the reader's memory constraints but premature to adopt until supported implementations exist for their serving stack.

claims.statement: The method replaces uniform low-bit quantization of the linear-attention (GDN) recurrent state with a model-wide mixed-precision allocation driven by quantization residuals and gradient sensitivity to future loss, plus an FP8 sliding window that keeps recent writes unquantized until they age out. Its cost is implementation complexity: per-head bit-width allocation, a separate FP8 write path that must be propagated through the full state transition, and merged on window exit, all of which require custom inference code for a specific architecture. It can fail when the deployed model is not a GDN-style linear-attention model, when gradient-sensitivity estimates do not transfer across tasks, or when the window merge introduces transition artifacts not covered by the seven evaluated tasks.

On Qwen3.5-4B/9B, GGA plus an FP8 pure-write sliding window reaches 69.83%/78.63% seven-task macro-averages, 38.39/41.21 percentage points above STEPQuant@4 at a comparable state-storage budget, while reducing mean generation length by 32.32%/36.77% relative to GGA@4 alone.
